Routing lessons:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected for every tested request, including large/small refunds, shipments, and claims across north, south, and east. Avoid C unless new evidence specifically supports it.
- Option B (priority desk) was rejected for a large claim from the east region. Do not assume urgency or a second attempt makes B valid.
- No successful selections yet; there is insufficient evidence to map request type, size, region, requester department, or note wording to A–D.
- Requester notes such as “urgent,” “second attempt,” “regional office,” or “no rush” did not establish a valid route. Use structured attributes (request type, size, region) and gather more evidence before choosing.

Routing lessons:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected for all tested requests, including varied refunds, shipments, and claims across north, south, and east. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option B (priority desk) was rejected for a large east claim. No successful B or D selections are known; do not infer validity from urgency, retries, or requester wording.
- Option A (standard queue) is confirmed valid for small refunds from the south region: accepted across Field Sales, Regional Ops, and Client Services, with both “no rush” and “regional office” notes.
- Option A was rejected for: small invoice/east, small claim/north, small shipment/south, large invoice/east, and small claim/south. Thus request type, size, and region matter; “regional office” wording does not require route C.
- Notes such as “second attempt,” scanned paperwork, urgency, or “no rush” have not reliably determined routing. Structured attributes remain more useful, but the mapping is incomplete.
- Current evidence supports choosing A only for the observed small-refund/south pattern (pending further confirmation). Gather more evidence before selecting routes for other combinations.

Routing lessons:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected for all tested requests across north, south, and east, including varied refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option D (external partner) was rejected for every tested request in steps 20–23 and 25–29, spanning refunds, claims, shipments, north/south/east, and small/large sizes. Do not select D based on requester type or wording.
- Option B (priority desk) was rejected for a large east claim. No successful B or D selections are known.
- Option A (standard queue) is confirmed valid only for the observed small-refund/south pattern, across Field Sales, Regional Ops, and Client Services, with varied notes including “no rush” and “regional office.”
- Option A was rejected for small invoice/east, small claim/north, small shipment/south, large invoice/east, small claim/south, and newly tested large refund/south. Thus size, request type, and region matter.
- Requester notes (“second attempt,” urgency, repeated follow-up, scanned paperwork, “no rush,” or “regional office”) have not reliably determined routing. Structured attributes remain more useful, but the mapping is incomplete.
- New tests also show D is not a fallback when A is uncertain or when requests are urgent, repeated, or submitted by Partner Accounts.
- Current evidence supports choosing A only for the confirmed small-refund/south pattern. Treat all other combinations as unresolved; gather evidence before selecting A, B, C, or D.

Routing lessons:
- Option C (regional office) remains rejected across tested north, south, and east requests involving refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option D (external partner) remains rejected across tested refunds, claims, shipments, regions, sizes, requester types, urgency, and follow-ups. Do not use D as a fallback.
- Option B (priority desk) is now confirmed valid for: large shipment/north, small claim/north, and large invoice/east.
- B was rejected for small refund/north, small shipment/north, large claim/south (tested twice), and previously large claim/east. Thus B depends on structured attributes; requester type and urgency are insufficient.
- Option A (standard queue) is confirmed only for the observed small-refund/south pattern, across Field Sales, Regional Ops, and Client Services, with varied notes.
- A was rejected for small invoice/east, small claim/north and south, small shipment/south, large invoice/east, large refund/south, small claim/east, and small refund/north. Do not generalize the confirmed A pattern.
- Requester notes such as regional-office origin, urgency, repeated follow-up, scanned paperwork, “no rush,” or prior similar requests do not reliably determine routing. Structured request attributes matter more, but the mapping is incomplete.
- Current evidence supports A only for small refund/south; supports B only for the three confirmed combinations above. Treat all other combinations as unresolved and gather evidence before selecting A, B, C, or D.

Routing lessons:
- Option C (regional office) remains rejected across tested north, south, and east requests involving refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option D (external partner) remains rejected across tested refunds, claims, shipments, regions, sizes, requester types, urgency, and follow-ups. Do not use D as a fallback.
- B (priority desk) is confirmed only for small claim/north (accepted again at step 48).
- Earlier B confirmations for large shipment/north and large invoice/east are contradicted by later rejections (steps 45 and 47). Treat both as unresolved rather than valid.
- B was also rejected for small refund/north, small shipment/north, large claim/south (repeated), and small claim/south. Do not infer routing from urgency or requester type.
- A (standard queue) remains confirmed only for the observed small-refund/south pattern, across Field Sales, Regional Ops, and Client Services, with varied notes.
- A is rejected for large claim/east (repeated), large claim/south, small invoice/east and south, small claim/north and south, small shipment/south, large invoice/east, large refund/south, and small refund/north. Do not generalize the small-refund/south result.
- Requester notes—regional-office origin, urgency, repeated follow-up, scanned paperwork, “no rush,” prior similar requests, or missing-information reminders—do not reliably determine routing. Structured attributes matter more, but the mapping is incomplete and may require repeated validation.
- Current safe knowledge: A only for small refund/south; B only for small claim/north. Treat every other combination as unresolved; gather evidence before selecting A, B, C, or D.

Routing lessons:
- C (regional office) remains rejected across tested north, south, and east requests involving refunds, shipments, and claims. Avoid C absent new evidence.
- D (external partner) remains rejected across tested refunds, claims, shipments, regions, sizes, requester types, urgency, and follow-ups. Do not use D as fallback.
- B (priority desk) is confirmed only for small claim/north (accepted at step 48). It is rejected for large shipment/north, large invoice/east, small refund/north, small shipment/north, large claim/south, small claim/south, large refund/south, and small invoice/east. Treat all other B mappings as unresolved.
- A (standard queue) was previously accepted for small refund/south, but this is now contradicted by rejections at steps 51–52; no longer treat it as confirmed.
- New A confirmations: small invoice/north (step 53) and small shipment/east (step 57). Do not generalize beyond these exact patterns.
- A remains rejected for large claim/east, large claim/south, small invoice/east and south, small claim/north and south, small shipment/south, large invoice/east, large refund/south, and small refund/north and south.
- Requester notes—regional-office origin, urgency, repeated follow-up, scanned paperwork, “no rush,” prior attempts, or missing-information reminders—do not reliably determine routing. Structured attributes matter more, but mappings remain incomplete and may need repeated validation.
- Safe confirmed knowledge: A for small invoice/north and small shipment/east; B for small claim/north. Treat every other combination as unresolved; gather evidence before selecting A, B, C, or D.
